title: Hoop Shoot trailer v2 (the 'Play for keeps' cut)

timing.frame_rule: Every boundary is round(t * 60) on the GLOBAL timeline, so parts tile exactly: a part's length is end_frame - start_frame (bars are 130.9 frames, not whole numbers).

cut.note: song bars 5-8 again, fading out over all 4 bars with a qsin curve to silence at 39.273 s

rhythm: Beat 4 of every bar is near-silent: the make lands on beat 3, the net settles through beat 4, the cut lands on the next beat 1.

parts.title: Create your hooper
parts.shot: The real opening flow, as a new player sees it: the neon splash, a tap on NEW GAME, and the NEW PLAYER card sliding in. A quick re-roll of the name with the die shows it's yours to make.

hits.what: The splash: neon wall and sign, music starts
Tap NEW GAME
Splash slides out, NEW PLAYER slides in (the silent beat)
NEW PLAYER card lands; text card in
Tap the die: PLAYER NAME re-rolls
Hometown re-rolls
Hold on the finished card

parts.capture: A fresh install (or a trailer save with no player). Splash → NEW GAME → NEW PLAYER, then two die taps. Record the touches at real speed and trim to the hits; about 6 s with handles.
notes: Pick a re-rolled name and hometown that read well on screen, and land on them on beat 2.3.
parts.cut_out: Cut on the downbeat as the hi-hats come in

parts.title: The courts
parts.shot: One court per bar, each landing on the downbeat: a wide flyover in the style of the area home backgrounds, but travelling sideways much further. Optional quick real shot cut in on beat 3.
parts.inside_each_bar: 1–2 flyover · 3 optional real make · 4 net settles (or the flyover keeps moving)
parts.capture: Per court: a horizontal camera move across the area at the home background's height and angle, with a wider travel, 2.5 s each, all moving the same direction (left to right) so the four cuts read as one long pan. Optional: a 1 s real make per court, centred on the net.
parts.text: PLAY FOR KEEPS ON EVERY COURT
parts.text_note: One line, held across all four courts
text_options: PLAY FOR KEEPS ON EVERY COURT
notes: Every court cut lands on a downbeat: 0:04.36, 0:06.55, 0:08.73, 0:10.91.
If a court gets a real make, land it on beat 3 and let the net settle through the silent beat 4.
Optional: a small court name in the corner changing on each downbeat (ARCADE CAGE, BEACH, PARK, CITY).

Ross, 2026-11-13, after seeing 2a-2d together: the four bars all cut pan -> live on the same beat and sat on the downbeat. 2a keeps its bar; the beach live shot is opened up by a second (2b = 393-589, beats 4.1 to 5.3, its swish on the bar-5 downbeat, 5.1: the recording was paused too soon after the swish to hold on it instead), paid for by the park and city pans (2c = 589-687 starting on 5.3, its swish on 5.4; 2d = 687-785 starting on 6.2, its make on 6.3). The part's own bounds (262-785) and the downbeat on 3.1 / the drop on 7.1 are unchanged.
parts.open_question: You said bars 3–7. I've ended this at the start of bar 7 (0:13.09), because bar 7 is where the drums drop. Four courts fill bars 3–6 exactly. Tell me if you want the City to carry into the drop.
parts.cut_out: Hard cut exactly on the drop

parts.title: Run the league
parts.shot: The drop lands on a league win: the YOU WIN page with its flash, rays and confetti. Then the CLINCHED page: your row hops up the standings and PLAYOFFS slams in.

hits.what: YOU WIN: the flash hits on the first drum hit
Text card in
Confetti, the score settles
Hold
CLINCHED page: the standings, mid-climb
Your row hops up into a playoff spot
PLAYOFFS slams in (gold rays)
CLINCHED · NO. 1 SEED settles

parts.capture: A league win on the final day that clinches a playoff spot, so the YOU WIN beat and the CLINCHED page come from the same run. In the game PLAYOFFS slams 2.5 s after the page opens and the climb runs before it: enter the CLINCHED clip about 1.1 s before the slam so the hop lands on 8.2 and the slam on 8.3.
notes: The game's own flash on YOU WIN is the drum hit; keep it on 0:13.09 exactly.
Let the text card come in a beat after the flash (8 frames or so) so the two don't fight.
Use a seed that reads as a reward: NO. 1 or NO. 2.

parts.title: Earn power-ups, set your loadout
parts.shot: The league page: tap the CARDS tab, buy a card from the SHOP with tickets, and it slides into your lineup. Then the pre-match LOADOUT: drag that card into a slot and it's set for the match.

hits.what: League page: tap the CARDS tab; text card in
Tap the card's ticket price
Card slides into the lineup
Hold on it in the lineup
Pre-match LOADOUT page
Drag the card toward an empty slot
It snaps into the slot, set
Hold on READY

parts.capture: A trailer save with tickets to spend. League page → CARDS tab → buy one card (pick one with a strong face, like Deep Freeze or Magnet) and catch it sliding into the lineup. Then a pre-match LOADOUT with that card dragged in. About 3 s each with handles.
notes: Use the same card in both halves so it reads as one card travelling from the shop to the match.
Both halves are touch-driven: do the taps a little early and trim so each lands on its beat.

Built 2026-11-13: Deep Freeze (the shop's first row; Magnet's row is below the pane's fold), staged out of the cage bucket so the buy grows a new slot in YOUR CARDS. The buy is the game's two taps (price -> X / CONFIRM -> buy): the price on 9.2, CONFIRM on 9.3 (the flight starts there), the land inside the 9.4 hold. The text card moves up at the cut (card_y).

card_y.why: The pre-match page's loadout slots sit under the locked slot (design y 1009-1138); from the cut the card sits in the gap between the OPPONENT panel and YOU (520-685), over the VS.

parts.title: Solo or online
parts.shot: Straight into a live online heat against a real player, from your POV. A close game in its last 15 seconds: the clock and the tight score visible, the opponent's picture-in-picture live in the corner.

hits.what: Cut in mid-heat, clock under 0:15, score within a basket or two; text card in
Your flick
Make: you go up by one
Net settles; the PiP shows them shooting back
Their make lands in the PiP: tied, or they lead
Your flick
Make: back in front
Hold: the clock running down, one point in it

parts.capture: An online match with a friend (friend code), both phones screen recording at 60 fps from before tip-off. From your recording: about 6 s in the last 15 s with the lead changing hands, two of your makes and one of theirs in the PiP.
notes: Play this match on the iPhone 16 yourself and give your friend the XR: your POV is on screen for about 5.5 s, theirs for about 2 s, so the sharper, smoother phone should carry yours.
This scene and the next come from the same match. Pick the stretch where the score is closest, then play the ice card a few seconds later (scene 6).
Keep both recordings whole; the ice card moment is what syncs the two POVs in the edit.

Built 2026-11-13 from Ross's XR recording (raw/part05/ross_pov.mov, conformed), clip frames 118-380: the clock 29.5 -> 25.2, YOU 18-19 -> 20-20; Deep Freeze fires at part frame 162 (just before 12.2) and, a second later, a 40-frame zip into the opponent's PiP runs from 222 to the last frame (Ross: the zoom at the end of part 5, a second after the card, not too fast), so part 6 opens in the friend's POV.

parts.title: Play your cards right
parts.shot: You play Deep Freeze at a critical point. The edit zips (a fast zoom) into the opponent's picture-in-picture and lands in their POV just as their rim ices over, then their next shot can't get through.

hits.what: Your POV: tap Deep Freeze; text card in
The card fires
The zip starts: a fast zoom into their PiP
Through the PiP (the silent beat)
Land in THEIR POV on the downbeat: the rim ices over, ICED BY CARD
They flick
The ball is caught by the ice
Hold on the frozen rim

parts.capture: Same match, at a moment that matters: the opponent about to tie or take the lead. From your recording: the card tap plus 1.5 s. From your friend's recording: 2.5 s starting just before their rim ices, through their next shot hitting the ice.
notes: Sync the two recordings on the ice: it shows up in your PiP and on their rim at the same moment.
The PiP draws a simplified court at half rate, so keep the zip quick and get into their real POV fast; that's where the picture is sharp.
Deep Freeze makes them swish through the ice, get caught, or rattle it three times. A shot caught by the ice on 14.3 is the clearest payoff.

Both phones: Do Not Disturb on, start the screen recording from Control Center before the match, and check the recording for the status bar or the red recording pill; crop or cover it in the edit if it shows.

Each phone lays the HUD out around its own notch or Dynamic Island, so the HUD sits slightly lower on the 16 than on the XR. On the zip into their POV that's expected: it's a different player's screen.

Built 2026-11-13 from the friend's recording (raw/part06/friend_pov.mov, conformed), its first 262 frames: their rim already iced, the card arriving, clock 25.4 -> 21.0; it opens zoomed x4 on their hoop and pulls back to the whole frame in 24 frames (the mirror of part 5's zip, Ross's call), so 13.1 is the land; they score through the ice twice in the part (21 -> 22 at 13.4/14.3).

parts.title: End card
parts.shot: The bare splash: the neon wall and sign with no buttons underneath. The App Store badge and an Android coming-soon line sit below the sign. Everything fades out together with the music.

hits.what: Cut to the bare splash, badges already in place
Hold
Whole frame starts fading as the music drops away
Black, as the music reaches silence at 0:39.27

parts.capture: A headless render of the splash with its buttons hidden (needs a small trailer option in the splash, since the real screen always shows them), about 5 s, then the badges and legal lines added in the edit.
notes: App Store badge: Apple's official black "Download on the App Store" badge, unmodified, placed first (left of or above any Android mark). It mustn't be animated on its own, so fade the whole frame rather than the badge. If the trailer goes out before the app is live, Apple's pre-order badge is the one to use.

Android: Google has no "coming soon" version of the Get it on Google Play badge, and the badge mustn't be altered. Either turn on pre-registration in the Play Console and use Google's official pre-registration badge, or write COMING SOON TO ANDROID in the game's font with no Google badge.

Legal lines, small at the bottom of the card: "Apple and the Apple logo are trademarks of Apple Inc., registered in the U.S. and other countries. App Store is a service mark of Apple Inc." Add "Google Play and the Google Play logo are trademarks of Google LLC." only if a Google badge is used. The music credit can go here too.
Keep clear space around the Apple badge of at least a quarter of its height.
parts.cut_out: end (fade to black with the music)
